narrativeProgression.description: The narrator explains the reaction is used to prepare aryl halides from diazonium salts.
The narrator explains the first step: reaction of aminobenzene (aniline) with nitrous acid in presence of NaNO2 + HCL at 273-278 Kelvin, yielding benzene diazonium chloride salt.
The narrator points out that the formed benzene diazonium salt is further used to prepare aryl halides.
The narrator focuses on the replacement of Nitrogen in the benzene diazonium salt.
The narrator lists Chlorine, Bromine and Cyano group as replacing agents for Nitrogen, and calls this the Sandmeyer reaction.
